subject: Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@fintechco.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 15:10:00 -0000
Subject: Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist / next steps

Hi Alex / Sarah —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from the demo and the follow-up items we discussed around performance and SLOs. Major takeaways we captured:

- Target latency: p95 target of ~200ms for request/response (non-streaming generation)
- Streaming: need end-to-end streaming for multi-turn assistants with token-level partials (low first-byte latency)
- Throughput & concurrency: baseline of 50 concurrent requests during peak with burst to 150 for short windows
- KV/cache expectations: long-running sessions (up to 30k tokens cached per user session)
- Failure tolerance: graceful degradation to smaller model variant with warm fallback under capacity constraints

Next steps (proposed MAP / mutual action plan):
1) You to confirm perf targets above and share any existing perf tests (we can baseline).
2) Redwood to provide SLO checklist + suggested load-test parameters and a sample run plan.
3) Align on decision criteria (latency P95, cost $/k tokens, successful streaming percent) and deadline for decision (you mentioned end of Oct).
4) Schedule a short run with our infra team next week to validate concurrency & streaming behavior.

I attached a copy of the rough SLO notes you asked for during the call — please share any perf artifacts you have (load test results, current SLAs).

Thanks —
Marissa
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Attachment: fintechco-current-slo.pdf (stub)

Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 15:45:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist / next steps

Thanks Marissa — great demo. Confirming the targets from our side with a few clarifications:

- Latency: p95 target of <= 200ms for single-shot generation at our typical prompt sizes (avg 120 tokens); p99 target is less critical but good to track.
- Streaming: first-byte latency < 50ms when streaming enabled; we rely on partial token delivery for UX.
- Concurrency/throughput: sustained 50 qps with ability to burst to 150 qps for up to 5 minutes. We expect peaks at midday US hours.
- Session caching: we commonly keep 20–30k tokens per session; ability to hot-cache partial KV is important.

Attached the high-level perf summary we ran last quarter — it’s coarse but should help baseline. Let us know what you need to reproduce.

Also, decision criteria from our side:
- Meets p95 latency target under production-like workload
- Streaming robustness (no token loss / correct ordering)
- Predictable unit cost (within the ballpark of your initial pricing)

I can confirm decision timeline: procurement and infra alignment targeted by Oct 29.

Alex
Head of Platform Engineering | FintechCo
alex.johnson@fintechco.com | (617) 555-0199

Attachment: fintechco-current-slo.pdf (stub)

Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist / next steps

Appreciate the quick confirmation, Alex. Attached is the SLO checklist + suggested load-test parameters (redwood-slo-checklist.xlsx). Summary of the checklist here for convenience:

SLO checklist (high level)
- Latency SLOs: p95 <= 200ms (single-shot), first-byte streaming < 50ms
- Availability: 99.9% request success rate measured over 30d window
- Streaming: >= 99% successful token stream delivery across sessions
- Fallback behavior: warm fallback to smaller model < 500ms additional latency when triggered
- KV cache hit rate target: >= 85% for hot sessions

Load-test parameters we recommend
- Baseline run: 50 concurrent sustained users for 30 minutes, avg prompt 120 tokens
- Burst run: ramp to 150 concurrent users over 30s, sustain 5 minutes, repeat 3x with cool-downs
- Streaming validation: 1:1 mapping of session to stream for 500 sessions, check first-byte and token ordering
- Failure injection: simulate 10% transient infra failure to validate graceful fallback

MAP items & owners
- FintechCo: share last 2 perf test artifacts and any internal SLAs (Alex) — due: 2026-10-07
- Redwood: schedule test run and provide pre-configured load harness (Rishi) — target run: 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-14
- Redwood CS (Monica): observe run and collect metrics for decision report — target: 2026-10-14

Decision criteria (recap)
- Meets p95 latency target under production-like workload
- Streaming works reliably at target concurrency (50 sustained, bursts to 150)
- Unit cost estimate acceptable to FintechCo procurement

If that looks right I’ll lock the test window and loop in our infra folks. Happy to adjust any of the load parameters if your infra team has constraints.

Thanks,
Marissa
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Attachment: redwood-slo-checklist.xlsx (stub)

Thanks all — looping in our infra lead Vivek to coordinate the run. Proposed plan:

- I’ll provision a pre-warmed test cluster matching the medium production profile and share access by EOD 10/09.
- We’ll run the baseline on 10/12 (50 sustained users) and run the burst tests 10/13–10/14.
- Monica will collect traces/metrics and I’ll produce a short decision report comparing p95 and streaming delivery against your artifact.

Alex — can you confirm you can share the perf artifacts by COB 10/07 and whether you prefer us to run tests in your staging or on a Redwood-hosted cluster? Either is fine — we can collaborate on test config.

-Rishi
